To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the euAPETALA3 (euAP3) motif was generated by a single-nucleotide deletion in the C-terminus of the ancestral APETALA3/TM6 protein, and that the frameshift mutation was associated with a few other nucleotide substitutions in the coding region.

(1) the euAP3 C-terminal motif is derived from the paleoAP3 C-terminal domain; (2) the euAP type C-terminal motif was created by a single nucleotide mutation that produced a frameshift; (3) the frameshift was associated with a very limited set of nucleotide substitutions; and (4) the euAP motif is evolving as coding sequence, not as a noncoding regulatory region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolutionary process of molecular innovation, which we have shown to have occurred at least twice in the lineage leading to the euAP3 genes.
how the evolution of a novel protein motif is associated with the evolution of novel function and the rapid fixation of that novel protein motif.
how a single nucleotide change can produce a novel protein motif that is conserved across the angiosperms and that may have been important in the diversification of the eudicot lineage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a frameshift mutation in a single gene has produced a new C-terminal motif that is now found in the majority of eudicots.
the euAPETALA3/TM6 lineage is the result of the most significant change in MADS domain evolution in the angiosperms.
the frameshift mutation was a key event in the evolution of the euAP2 subclade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AP3 lineage is a good example of how a relatively simple change in DNA sequence can lead to the evolution of a new protein function.

the euAPETALA3 (euAP3) lineage is the most ancient and widespread of the type II MADS domain gene lineages in the eudicot clade, and that it has been the most extensively studied of all MADS box gene lineages.
a single nucleotide insertion in the APETLA3 lineage resulted in the creation of a novel protein domain that is now found in all eudicots.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frameshift event was not a random mutation, but rather was the first step in a process of molecular evolution that has been ongoing for at least 100 million years.
a simple genetic event can produce a novel protein sequence that is conserved in a phylogenetically diverse group of plants.

the frameshift mutation in the euAP3 lineage was not accompanied by the accumulation of many other mutations in the coding sequence, which suggests that the new motif is under strong selective constraint.
